newsitem.title: INDIA: Shipping resumes at Calcutta after sinking.
newsitem.headline: Shipping resumes at Calcutta after sinking.

text.p: Normal shipping operations resumed from Calcutta port on Saturday, two days after a Panama-flag cargo ship carrying 7,000 tonnes of steel sank in a river near the city, a port official said.
Three cargo ships and two small oil tankers sailed out after midnight, a spokesman for the Calcutta Port Trust (CPT) told Reuters.
The ship, the Green Opal, on its way to Hong Kong, sank in the Hooghly river after hitting a barge about 40 km from Calcutta on Thursday.
"Five ships will arrive at the Calcutta dock during the day on Saturday," the spokesman said.
Movements to and from Haldia dock, including the two oil jetties, were unaffected. The state-owned Indian Oil Corp has a 2.75 million tonne crude oil refinery at Haldia.
"We have approached the owner of the vessel, Doo Yang Lines Co Ltd, Seoul, for immediate removal of the wreckage," the spokesman said.
